newsitem.title: USA: Oregon extends comment period on Enron, PGE merger.
newsitem.headline: Oregon extends comment period on Enron, PGE merger.

text.p: The Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC) will delay finalizing a revised schedule for reviewing the planned merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co until late March, a spokesman for the commission said Wednesday.
An OPUC administrative law judge decided Wednesday to accept intervenor comments on the case until March 27, and is unlikely to set a new review schedule until after April 1.

Under a tentative schedule agreed to during failed settlement discussions last week, the OPUC staff was expected to submit a report on the merger by April 11 and a final commission decision was scheduled for June 4.
But the possible need for "factual evidentiary hearings," as Enron and Portland General have suggested, would "fundamentally change the nature" of the OPUC proceeding, according to the judge.
As a result, he decided to open the issue to comments from outside intervenors such as Citizens' Utility Board of Oregon and Industrial Customers of Northwest Utilities.
The companies met a week ago with staff of the commission in Salem to work out differences over how much of a rate cut utility customers should be guaranteed following the merger.
Enron was said to offer as much as $108 million, including $9 million a year for four years in cost savings.
The commission staff is holding out for a cut of $141 million, including the same $9 million for four years in cost of service reductions.
